sections.title: Solubility product and the Ksp-to-solubility table

board_events.text: From Ksp to molar solubility
AB type, like silver chloride: $K_{sp}=s^2$, so $s=\sqrt{K_{sp}}$.
A2B or AB2 type, like calcium fluoride: $K_{sp}=4s^3$, so $s=(K_{sp}/4)^{1/3}$.
AB3 type, like iron hydroxide: $K_{sp}=27s^4$, so $s=(K_{sp}/27)^{1/4}$.
The rule of thumb: read the subscripts, then choose the matching root — never blindly take the square root.
K s p carries units of molar raised to the total number of ions.

segments.text: The solubility product connects to molar solubility through a small table you must know by type.

For a general salt A x B y, the dissolution gives x of the cation and y of the anion, so the solubility product is the cation concentration to the power x times the anion concentration to the power y.
For an A B type, like silver chloride, the solubility product is s squared, so the solubility s is just the square root of K s p.
For an A two B or A B two type, like calcium fluoride, the solubility product is four s cubed, so s is the cube root of K s p over four.
For an A B three type, like iron hydroxide, the solubility product is twenty seven s to the fourth, so s is the fourth root of K s p over twenty seven.
The rule of thumb is to read the subscripts first and then choose the matching root, and never blindly take the square root.
And remember K s p carries units of molar raised to the total number of ions in the formula.
Solubility product molar solubility से एक छोटी table के ज़रिए जुड़ता है जो आपको type के हिसाब से आनी चाहिए।
एक general salt A x B y के लिए dissolution x cation और y anion देता है, इसलिए solubility product है cation concentration to the power x into anion concentration to the power y।
A B type के लिए, जैसे silver chloride, solubility product है s squared, इसलिए solubility s बस K s p का square root है।
A two B या A B two type के लिए, जैसे calcium fluoride, solubility product है four s cubed, इसलिए s है cube root of K s p over four।
A B three type के लिए, जैसे iron hydroxide, solubility product है twenty seven s to the fourth, इसलिए s है fourth root of K s p over twenty seven।
Rule of thumb यह है कि पहले subscripts पढ़िए और फिर मिलता-जुलता root चुनिए, और कभी आँख मूँदकर square root मत लीजिए।
और याद रखिए K s p, molar raised to formula में कुल ions की संख्या के units रखता है।

sections.title: Precipitation criterion and salt-hydrolysis pH

board_events.text: When it precipitates, and how salts tip pH
The ionic product Q is the same expression built from current concentrations.
Weak acid + strong base is basic: $\mathrm{pH}=7+\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{p}K_a+\log c)$.
Strong acid + weak base is acidic: $\mathrm{pH}=7-\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{p}K_b+\log c)$.
The half-p-K term is always positive, so the solution always leans toward the stronger parent's side.

segments.text: Two more relations finish the toolkit: one decides precipitation, the other gives the pH of a salt.

For precipitation, compare the ionic product Q with the solubility product: if Q is greater than K s p a precipitate forms, if they are equal the solution is just saturated, and if Q is less than K s p it is unsaturated.
Here the ionic product Q is exactly the same expression as K s p, but built from the current concentrations rather than the equilibrium ones.

For hydrolysis, the hydrolysis constant K h equals the water constant over K a for a weak-acid strong-base salt, or over K b for a strong-acid weak-base salt, and the degree of hydrolysis h is the square root of K h over c.
A weak-acid strong-base salt is basic, with pH equal to seven plus one half times the quantity p K a plus log c.
A strong-acid weak-base salt is acidic, with pH equal to seven minus one half times the quantity p K b plus log c.
In each case the half-p-K term is positive, which is why the solution always leans toward the side of its stronger parent.
दो और relations toolkit पूरा करती हैं: एक precipitation तय करती है, दूसरी salt का pH देती है।

Precipitation के लिए ionic product Q की solubility product से तुलना कीजिए: अगर Q, K s p से बड़ा है तो precipitate बनता है, बराबर हों तो solution बस saturated है, और Q, K s p से छोटा हो तो unsaturated।
यहाँ ionic product Q बिलकुल K s p जैसा ही expression है, पर equilibrium की जगह current concentrations से बना है।

Hydrolysis के लिए hydrolysis constant K h बराबर water constant over K a, weak-acid strong-base salt के लिए, या over K b, strong-acid weak-base salt के लिए, और degree of hydrolysis h बराबर square root of K h over c।
Weak-acid strong-base salt basic होता है, pH बराबर seven plus one half into p K a plus log c।
Strong-acid weak-base salt acidic होता है, pH बराबर seven minus one half into p K b plus log c।
हर case में half-p-K term positive है, इसीलिए solution हमेशा अपने stronger parent की side की ओर झुकता है।

sections.title: Worked example — pH of a basic buffer (CBSE)

board_events.text: Equal amounts, so pH is fixed by pKb
Find the pH of a buffer that is 0.10 molar in ammonia and 0.10 molar in ammonium chloride, with K b of 1.8 times ten to the minus five.
A basic buffer sits on the basic side of seven, exactly as expected.
The equal-amounts case collapses the log term to zero, so pH is set by p K b alone.

segments.text: This Board-level example is a one-liner because the buffer has equal amounts of base and salt.
We want the pH of a buffer that is zero point one zero molar in ammonia and zero point one zero molar in ammonium chloride, with K b equal to one point eight times ten to the minus five.
Use the basic-buffer form: pOH equals p K b plus the log of salt over base, and since salt and base are equal, the log of one is zero, leaving pOH equal to p K b.
Now p K b is minus the log of one point eight times ten to the minus five, which is four point seven four, so pOH is four point seven four.
Then the pH is fourteen minus four point seven four, which is nine point two six.
A basic buffer sits on the basic side of seven, which is exactly what we expect.
The key insight is that the equal-amounts case collapses the log term to zero, so the pH is set by p K b alone.
यह Board-level example एक line का है क्योंकि buffer में base और salt बराबर मात्रा में हैं।
हमें चाहिए एक buffer का pH जो zero point one zero molar in ammonia और zero point one zero molar in ammonium chloride है, K b बराबर one point eight times ten to the minus five के साथ।
Basic-buffer form इस्तेमाल कीजिए: pOH बराबर p K b plus log of salt over base, और चूँकि salt और base बराबर हैं, log of one zero है, जिससे pOH बराबर p K b बचता है।
अब p K b है minus log of one point eight times ten to the minus five, यानी four point seven four, तो pOH है four point seven four।
फिर pH है fourteen minus four point seven four, यानी nine point two six।
Basic buffer seven की basic side पर बैठता है, जो बिलकुल हमारी उम्मीद है।
मुख्य बात यह है कि बराबर-मात्रा वाला case log term को zero कर देता है, इसलिए pH अकेले p K b से तय होता है।

sections.title: Worked example — solubility of silver chromate (NEET speed trap)

board_events.text: Read the subscripts before the root
The solubility product of silver chromate is 1.1 times ten to the minus twelve; find its molar solubility.
The trap: taking the square root of K s p, because silver chromate is a one-to-two salt, not one-to-one.
So the solubility is about six point five times ten to the minus five molar.
Speed cue: the square root is only for A B salts; A two B salts need the cube root of K s p over four.

segments.text: This N E E T trap punishes reaching for the square root without checking the formula.
The solubility product of silver chromate is one point one times ten to the minus twelve, and we want its molar solubility.
The reflex trap is to take the square root of the solubility product, but that is wrong, because silver chromate is a one-to-two salt, not a one-to-one salt.
The correct expression is the solubility product equals four s cubed, so s is the cube root of the solubility product over four.
Putting in the number, s is the cube root of one point one times ten to the minus twelve over four, which is the cube root of two point seven five times ten to the minus thirteen.
That works out to about six point five times ten to the minus five molar.
The speed cue is permanent: the square root is only for an A B salt; an A two B salt needs the cube root of the solubility product over four.
यह N E E T trap formula check किए बिना square root पकड़ने पर सज़ा देता है।
Silver chromate का solubility product है one point one times ten to the minus twelve, और हमें उसकी molar solubility चाहिए।
Reflex trap है solubility product का square root लेना, पर यह ग़लत है, क्योंकि silver chromate एक one-to-two salt है, one-to-one नहीं।
सही expression है solubility product बराबर four s cubed, इसलिए s है cube root of solubility product over four।
Number रखने पर s है cube root of one point one times ten to the minus twelve over four, यानी cube root of two point seven five times ten to the minus thirteen।
यह निकलता है लगभग six point five times ten to the minus five molar।
Speed cue पक्का है: square root सिर्फ़ A B salt के लिए है; A two B salt को cube root of solubility product over four चाहिए।

sections.subtopic: Buffers, Solubility Product (Ksp) & Salt Hydrolysis
sections.title: Worked example — pH of a hydrolysing salt (JEE Main)

board_events.text: Sodium acetate is basic
Calculate the pH of a 0.10 molar sodium acetate solution, with K a of acetic acid at 1.8 times ten to the minus five.
Sodium acetate is a weak-acid strong-base salt, so it hydrolyses to give a basic solution.
Cross-check: pH equals seven plus one half times p K a plus log c, which also gives eight point eight seven.

segments.text: This J E E Main example applies the hydrolysis machinery to a common salt.
We want the pH of a zero point one zero molar sodium acetate solution, with the K a of acetic acid equal to one point eight times ten to the minus five.
Sodium acetate is the salt of a weak acid and a strong base, so its acetate ion hydrolyses to give a basic solution.

First the hydrolysis constant K h equals the water constant over K a, which is ten to the minus fourteen over one point eight times ten to the minus five, giving five point six times ten to the minus ten.
Then the hydroxide concentration is the square root of K h times c, which is the square root of five point six times ten to the minus eleven, giving seven point five times ten to the minus six molar.
So the pOH is five point one three, and the pH is fourteen minus that, which is eight point eight seven.
As a cross-check, the direct formula, pH equals seven plus one half times p K a plus log c, also gives eight point eight seven.
यह J E E Main example hydrolysis machinery को एक आम salt पर लगाता है।
हमें चाहिए zero point one zero molar sodium acetate solution का pH, acetic acid का K a बराबर one point eight times ten to the minus five के साथ।
Sodium acetate एक weak acid और strong base का salt है, इसलिए इसका acetate ion hydrolyse होकर basic solution देता है।
पहले hydrolysis constant K h बराबर water constant over K a, यानी ten to the minus fourteen over one point eight times ten to the minus five, देता है five point six times ten to the minus ten।
फिर hydroxide concentration है square root of K h into c, यानी square root of five point six times ten to the minus eleven, देता है seven point five times ten to the minus six molar।
तो pOH है five point one three, और pH है fourteen minus वो, यानी eight point eight seven।
Cross-check के तौर पर direct formula, pH बराबर seven plus one half into p K a plus log c, भी eight point eight seven देता है।

sections.subtopic: Buffers, Solubility Product (Ksp) & Salt Hydrolysis
sections.title: Worked example — common-ion suppression of solubility (JEE Advanced)

board_events.text: Silver chloride in salt water
With K s p of silver chloride at 1.8 times ten to the minus ten, find its solubility in pure water and in 0.10 molar sodium chloride.
In sodium chloride the chloride from the salt swamps the trace from silver chloride, so chloride is about 0.10 molar.
The common chloride ion has made silver chloride about seven thousand four hundred times less soluble.

segments.text: This Advanced example makes the common-ion effect on solubility fully quantitative.
Given the solubility product of silver chloride as one point eight times ten to the minus ten, we find its solubility both in pure water and in zero point one zero molar sodium chloride.
In pure water, the solubility product equals s squared, so s is the square root of one point eight times ten to the minus ten, giving one point three four times ten to the minus five molar.
In sodium chloride, the chloride from the salt completely swamps the trace from the silver chloride, so the chloride concentration is about zero point one zero molar.

Then the new solubility s prime equals the solubility product over the chloride concentration, which is one point eight times ten to the minus ten over zero point one zero, giving one point eight times ten to the minus nine molar.
So the suppression factor is s over s prime, which is one point three four times ten to the minus five over one point eight times ten to the minus nine, about seven thousand four hundred.

So the common chloride ion has made silver chloride roughly seven thousand four hundred times less soluble, which is exactly why gravimetric precipitates are washed with a dilute common-ion solution rather than pure water.
यह Advanced example solubility पर common-ion effect को पूरी तरह quantitative बना देता है।
Silver chloride का solubility product one point eight times ten to the minus ten दिया है, हम उसकी solubility pure water और zero point one zero molar sodium chloride दोनों में निकालते हैं।
Pure water में solubility product बराबर s squared, तो s है square root of one point eight times ten to the minus ten, देता है one point three four times ten to the minus five molar।
Sodium chloride में salt से आया chloride, silver chloride से आई trace को पूरी तरह दबा देता है, तो chloride concentration लगभग zero point one zero molar है।

फिर new solubility s prime बराबर solubility product over chloride concentration, यानी one point eight times ten to the minus ten over zero point one zero, देता है one point eight times ten to the minus nine molar।
तो suppression factor है s over s prime, यानी one point three four times ten to the minus five over one point eight times ten to the minus nine, लगभग seven thousand four hundred।

तो common chloride ion ने silver chloride को क़रीब seven thousand four hundred गुना कम soluble बना दिया, यही वजह है कि gravimetric precipitates को pure water की जगह dilute common-ion solution से धोया जाता है।

sections.subtopic: Buffers, Solubility Product (Ksp) & Salt Hydrolysis
sections.title: Traps and pro-tips for buffers, Ksp and hydrolysis

board_events.text: The four slips that flip answers
Do not assume every salt solution is neutral; only a strong-plus-strong salt is.
Do not use the plain square root for non-one-to-one salts; calcium fluoride needs four s cubed, iron hydroxide twenty seven s to the fourth.
On mixing equal volumes, halve every concentration before computing Q — this silently flips many precipitation answers.
Plug the ratio into Henderson, not absolute amounts; volume cancels, so moles work fine.
Pro-tip: for buffers, pH equals p K a at the half-equivalence point, and dilution barely moves buffer pH.
For hydrolysis, classify the salt first, then apply the one-line pH formula for its type.

segments.text: Let us close the chapter's numerical heartland with the four slips that flip answers.
First, do not assume every salt solution is neutral; only a strong-acid plus strong-base salt is neutral, so always identify the parents first.
Second, do not use the plain square root for a salt that is not one-to-one; calcium fluoride needs four s cubed, and iron hydroxide needs twenty seven s to the fourth.
Third, when you mix equal volumes, halve every concentration before computing the ionic product Q, because this step silently flips many precipitation answers.
Fourth, plug the ratio into Henderson, not the absolute amounts, since the volume cancels and moles work just as well as molarities.
Now a pro-tip: for buffers, remember that the pH equals p K a at the half-equivalence point, and that dilution barely moves a buffer's pH.
<whisper> And for hydrolysis, skip the full derivation entirely: classify the salt first, then just apply the one-line pH formula for its type.
चलिए chapter के numerical दिल को उन चार slips के साथ बंद करते हैं जो answers पलट देती हैं।
पहली, यह मत मानिए कि हर salt solution neutral है; सिर्फ़ strong-acid plus strong-base salt neutral होता है, इसलिए पहले parents पहचानिए।
दूसरी, जो salt one-to-one नहीं है उसके लिए सादा square root मत इस्तेमाल कीजिए; calcium fluoride को four s cubed चाहिए, और iron hydroxide को twenty seven s to the fourth।
तीसरी, जब आप बराबर volumes mix करें, ionic product Q निकालने से पहले हर concentration को आधा कीजिए, क्योंकि यह step चुपचाप कई precipitation answers पलट देता है।
चौथी, Henderson में ratio डालिए, absolute amounts नहीं, क्योंकि volume cancel हो जाता है और moles भी molarities जितने ही काम करते हैं।
अब एक pro-tip: buffers के लिए याद रखिए कि half-equivalence point पर pH बराबर p K a, और dilution buffer के pH को मुश्किल से हिलाता है।
<whisper> और hydrolysis के लिए पूरी derivation छोड़ दीजिए: पहले salt classify कीजिए, फिर उसके type के लिए बस one-line pH formula लगाइए।

sections.subtopic: Chapter Close — Formula Recap & Cheat Sheet
sections.title: Formula recap — the whole chapter at a glance

board_events.text: Every key relation, in order

segments.text: Here is the whole chapter's formula set, in the order we built it, to lock before the exam.
The law of mass action: K c is the product concentrations over the reactant concentrations, each raised to its coefficient.
The pressure link: K p equals K c times R T raised to delta n, where delta n counts gaseous product moles minus gaseous reactant moles.
The Gibbs bridge: delta G standard equals minus R T ln K, so K equals e to the power minus delta G standard over R T.
The van't Hoff equation: the log of K two over K one equals minus delta H standard over R, times one over T two minus one over T one.
The dissociation shortcut: K p equals alpha squared P over one minus alpha squared, for a single reactant giving two gases.
Water and pH: K w equals hydrogen ion times hydroxide ion, ten to the minus fourteen, and pH plus pOH equals fourteen.
Weak acids: alpha equals the square root of K a over c, the hydrogen-ion concentration is the square root of K a times c, and for a conjugate pair K a times K b equals K w.
Buffers: the Henderson equation, pH equals p K a plus the log of salt over acid.
And solubility: for an A B salt s is the square root of K s p, for an A two B or A B two salt K s p is four s cubed, and comparing Q with K s p decides precipitation.
यह पूरे chapter का formula set है, उसी क्रम में जैसे हमने बनाया, exam से पहले पक्का करने के लिए।
Law of mass action: K c है product concentrations over reactant concentrations, हर एक अपने coefficient की power पर।
Pressure link: K p बराबर K c into R T raised to delta n, जहाँ delta n गिनता है gaseous product moles minus gaseous reactant moles।
Gibbs bridge: delta G standard बराबर minus R T ln K, इसलिए K बराबर e to the power minus delta G standard over R T।
Van't Hoff equation: log of K two over K one बराबर minus delta H standard over R, into one over T two minus one over T one।
Dissociation shortcut: K p बराबर alpha squared P over one minus alpha squared, एक reactant से दो gases के लिए।
Water और pH: K w बराबर hydrogen ion into hydroxide ion, ten to the minus fourteen, और pH plus pOH बराबर fourteen।
Weak acids: alpha बराबर square root of K a over c, hydrogen-ion concentration है square root of K a into c, और conjugate pair के लिए K a into K b बराबर K w।
Buffers: Henderson equation, pH बराबर p K a plus log of salt over acid।
और solubility: A B salt के लिए s है square root of K s p, A two B या A B two salt के लिए K s p है four s cubed, और Q की K s p से तुलना precipitation तय करती है।

sections.subtopic: Chapter Close — Formula Recap & Cheat Sheet
sections.title: Cheat sheet — quick rules and memory aids

board_events.text: One-glance rules for the exam
Only temperature changes K; catalyst, pressure, inert gas and concentration never do.
Direction from Q: Q low, go; Q high, bye. Extent: $K \gt 10^{3}$ products win, $K \lt 10^{-3}$ reactants win.
Combining toolkit: reverse inverts, multiply powers, add multiplies.
Gibbs and heat: negative G means big K; hotter helps the endo.
Le Chatelier: the system fights the change; fewer moles win under pressure; catalyst is speed, not yield.
Ionic: acid gives pH under seven, base over seven; dilution nudges toward seven but never across.
Salts and salts: salt sides with the strong parent; read the subscripts before the root; equal is best for buffers.

segments.text: Finally, the cheat sheet: the one-glance rules and memory aids that carry the whole chapter.
First and biggest: only temperature changes the value of K; a catalyst, pressure, an inert gas, and concentration never do.
For direction, use Q low, go and Q high, bye; and for extent, K above ten to the power three means products win, while K below ten to the power minus three means reactants win.
For combining equilibria, remember the toolkit rhyme: reverse inverts, multiply powers, add multiplies.
For Gibbs energy and heat: a negative standard Gibbs change means a big K, and hotter helps the endothermic reaction.
For Le Chatelier: the system fights the change, fewer moles win under pressure, and a catalyst is speed, not yield.
For ionic equilibrium: an acid gives a pH under seven and a base over seven, and dilution nudges the pH toward seven but never across it.
